citation: Primary sources opened this session: (1) Jim Harter, Gallup, 'Span of control: optimal team size for managers', 13 Jan 2026, gallup.com/workplace/700718/span-control-optimal-team-size-managers.aspx. (2) Salvucci and Taatgen, 'Threaded Cognition: An Integrated Theory of Concurrent Multitasking', Psychological Review 115(1), 2008, 101-130, ai.rug.nl/~niels/publications/ThreadedCognitionPublished.pdf. (3) Steve Yegge, Gas Town README, github.com/steveyegge/gastown. (4) Bedard, Kropp, Hsu, Karaman, Hawes, Rosen Kellerman (BCG), 'When Using AI Leads to Brain Fry', HBR, 5 Mar 2026, hbr.org/2026/03/when-using-ai-leads-to-brain-fry (only the opening was retrievable). (5) Claude Code docs 'Common workflows', code.claude.com/docs/en/common-workflows.
source_tier: Gallup: consultancy research. Salvucci and Taatgen: peer-reviewed. Gas Town README: practitioner/vendor project documentation. HBR/BCG: consultancy research published in a magazine. Claude Code docs: company documentation.

sponsor_and_incentive: Gallup sells manager-development consulting and engagement surveys. BCG sells AI transformation consulting. Yegge builds and promotes Gas Town. Anthropic sells Claude Code. None is a neutral party on agent counts.
exact_quotes: Gallup: 'The average number of people reporting to managers has increased from 10.9 in 2024 to 12.1 in 2025.' 'the median team size has held steady at about five to six employees per manager or leader.' 'there is roughly one manager for every 11.5 employees.' Gallup states the ideal span 'isn't universal' (the fetch tool paraphrased this; verbatim wording not confirmed) [uncertain]. Gas Town README, table 'What Problem Does This Solve?': '4-10 agents become chaotic' against 'Scale comfortably to 20-30 agents'; Problems View section: 'At scale (20-50+ agents), spotting stuck agents in the activity stream becomes difficult.' Salvucci and Taatgen abstract: 'performing 2 or more tasks at once. Threaded cognition posits that streams of thought can be represented as threads of processing coordinated by a serial procedural resource...'. Claude Code docs: 'Run the same command with a different name in a second terminal to start an isolated parallel session.' HBR opening quote of an early Gas Town user: 'Gas Town was moving too fast for me.' The HBR sentence 'Just as we have norms for spans of control for managing humans, so, too, limits need to be defined for human + agent oversight' appears in the earlier file BCG_HBR_Brain_Fry.json but was not re-verified here [uncertain].
date_and_recency: Gallup 13 Jan 2026 (2024 and 2025 data). Salvucci and Taatgen 2008. HBR 5 Mar 2026. Gas Town README current at fetch (Oct 2026); Gas Town launched 1 Jan 2026 per HBR opening. Claude Code docs current at fetch.
key_claims: No source found sets an evidence-based limit on agents per person. Gallup: span of control is not universal and depends on context; it gives no single optimal number. Salvucci and Taatgen: multitasking interference arises from resource conflicts among concurrent threads, so there is no fixed task count. Gas Town README: 4-10 agents become chaotic without orchestration, 20-30 agents are manageable with its tooling, 20-50+ makes spotting stuck agents hard. Claude Code docs: describe running parallel sessions via worktrees and an agent view to monitor them, and state no recommended number or limit. HBR: calls for limits to be defined but (as far as retrieved) offers no number for agents per person.
headline_figures: Gallup: 10.9 (2024) to 12.1 (2025) average direct reports; median team five to six; 37% of managers oversee fewer than five, 66% fewer than 10, 22% 10 to 24, 13% 25 or more; BLS roughly one manager per 11.5 employees; managers spend a median 40% of time on individual contributor work. Gas Town README: 4-10 agents chaotic; 20-30 comfortable; 20-50+ stuck-agent detection difficult. Gallup: 'Highly engaged teams of 12 or more workers who are supported by effective management' can thrive (fetch-tool wording, [uncertain] verbatim). Secondary only, not opened at primary: Yegge stage 6 = 3 to 5 parallel agents, stage 7 = 10+ hand-managed, stage 8 = own orchestrator [uncertain]; BCG 'more than three AI tools' dip in productivity [uncertain]; Lattice 5.1 reports per manager; Bain 6-7 span [uncertain].
sample_unit_and_population: Gallup: US managers and leaders across occupations, not software engineers; human direct reports only. Salvucci and Taatgen: computational model of laboratory dual tasks and driving, not agent oversight. Gas Town: vendor-stated figures from Yegge's own tool, no sample. HBR/BCG: survey of 1,488 US workers per secondary summaries [uncertain], not engineering-specific.
observed_vs_stated: Gallup: survey/administrative data on team sizes (observed structure). Salvucci and Taatgen: model simulations compared to lab data. Gas Town README: author's stated experience, not measured. HBR/BCG: self-reported survey.
what_makes_oversight_tiring: Salvucci and Taatgen: concurrent threads compete for shared resources coordinated by a serial procedural resource; conflict produces interference (read in abstract; working-memory bottleneck detail from a secondary Taatgen summary [uncertain]). Gas Town README: stuck agents become hard to spot in a stream as counts rise. HBR: early user stress at the pace of agents (quote above).
consequence_for_quality: Not established for agent counts by any primary source opened. HBR/BCG reports errors and intent to quit linked to oversight load, but those figures were not re-verified here [uncertain].
what_reduces_the_load: Gas Town README: persistent work state, mailboxes, a problems view that surfaces agents needing intervention. Claude Code docs: worktrees isolate edits; agent view monitors parallel sessions from one screen. Gallup: span should be set by context, with manager support. None is validated by outcome data.
limitations_stated: Gallup says the ideal span depends on context and is not universal. Gas Town README is a product description with no evaluation. Salvucci and Taatgen model specific lab tasks, not supervisory work.
counter_evidence: Human span-of-control data is about managing people who self-direct, and does not transfer to agents that need checking of output. Gallup finds high-engagement teams of 12 or more can work, which cuts against a tight numeric cap. Temporal's State of Development 2026 (in Temporal_agents_per_person.json) reports no correlation between agent count and issue frequency, vendor survey. Gas Town's 20-30 claim conflicts with its own 4-10 chaos claim unless tooling is assumed.
verification_status: Checked against opened primary: Gallup figures; Gas Town README figures; Claude Code docs having no stated limit; Salvucci and Taatgen abstract. NOT checked: HBR span-of-control sentence [uncertain]; Yegge stage definitions and counts [uncertain]; BCG three-tools figure [uncertain]; Gartner span figures (no Gartner source found) [uncertain]; Anthropic best-practices, OpenAI Codex and GitHub guidance on parallel sessions not searched or opened [uncertain].
usable_claim: No published research or vendor guidance found sets a number of agents one person can safely oversee. Human span-of-control data (Gallup: median five to six reports, average 12.1 in 2025) shows spans are set by context, not a universal figure, so a leader's agent limit has to be a local rule, not a cited standard. Gas Town's own README says 4-10 agents becomes chaotic without orchestration tooling.
do_not_use: Any 'optimal span is N' claim; Gartner figures (none found); Yegge stage-to-agent-count mapping (secondary only); BCG 'three tools' and 39% figures (secondary only); Deloitte or Hyring Fortune 500 span figures (unverified); Temporal's median 5.0 agents as a safe limit (it is usage, not a limit); any mapping of Salvucci and Taatgen to a count of agents.
overlap_with_existing_essays: Not checked against the trust essay, Verification Gap or Checking Isn't Catching in this task [uncertain]. Brain-fry quote is already in BCG_HBR_Brain_Fry.json.
